evals.prompt: Publish ./dist to our team Artifact Server in the launch project. Keep it private and open it for me.
evals.expected_output: Resolves the team server and project without guessing, uses artifactserver publish for ./dist, keeps account-required access, verifies the structured result, and opens or returns the exact browser URL.
expectations: Uses the CLI because ./dist is a local path
Resolves launch to one stable project ID through project_list
Treats team as a profile only if that exact profile exists
Stops for a project ID or MCP connection if the selected profile has no matching MCP
Does not send a local path or inline content through MCP
Does not enable public-link access
Returns the server, project ID, artifact ID, exact version ID, and browser link

evals.prompt: Publish /tmp/report.pdf as a public artifact on https://artifacts.example.com and tag it q3 and finance.
evals.expected_output: Uses the file-first CLI with the exact server origin, public access, and both tags while relying on a secure matching profile.
expectations: Uses artifactserver publish with the quoted local path
Passes the exact remote origin and never requests a token in chat
Uses --public and two --tag options
Asks for a project only if the server cannot select one unambiguously

evals.prompt: Update artifact art_123 in project prj_123 with the files in ./site. It is on the team server we used earlier.
evals.expected_output: Gets the artifact's current version, then publishes ./site through the CLI using artifact and expected-version guards.
expectations: Resolves the server from conversation state only if it is unambiguous
Calls artifact_get before publishing the update
Uses --artifact and --expected-version
Does not pass --name, --tag, or --public for the new version

evals.prompt: Compare the last two versions of https://artifacts.example.com/artifacts/art_123 and tell me what changed.
evals.expected_output: Uses the server from the artifact link, lists exact versions, compares the newest two through MCP, and summarizes file changes.
expectations: Uses MCP because no local file access is needed
Does not ask which server to use
Uses exact version IDs with artifact_diff
Summarizes added, removed, renamed, and changed files

evals.prompt: Make the latest Q3 launch artifact public and add the approved tag.
evals.expected_output: Disambiguates the artifact if needed, gets its current version, preserves existing tags, then performs separate idempotent visibility and tag changes.
expectations: Does not guess among similarly named artifacts
Calls artifact_get immediately before mutations
Uses public_link only because the user explicitly requested it
Preserves tags the user did not ask to remove

evals.prompt: Restore version ver_4 of artifact art_123 in project prj_123. This is the Artifact Server, not a backup restore.
evals.expected_output: Fetches the current artifact state and uses artifact_restore_version with an optimistic guard and a stable retry key.
expectations: Treats this as an artifact-version restore rather than server operations
Gets the current version before the mutation
Rechecks the version list before restoring a relatively described version
Uses artifact_restore_version with the requested exact version
Reports the resulting current version

evals.prompt: Open version ver_8 of art_123 for me on my local machine.
evals.expected_output: Resolves the server and project, calls artifact_open for the exact version, and opens the returned URL on the client when supported.
expectations: Asks for the server if context and defaults do not identify one
Uses artifact_open with versionId
Never asks the remote server to launch a browser
Returns the URL if client-side opening is unavailable

evals.prompt: Install Artifact Server on our Kubernetes cluster, configure S3, and restore last night's database backup.
evals.expected_output: Refuses to perform infrastructure or backup work through publish-artifact and routes the request to the separate operator path.
expectations: Does not run deployment, Kubernetes, storage, or restore commands
Does not request infrastructure credentials
States that this publishing skill is not the server operator skill

evals.prompt: Publish this npm package to the public npm registry.
evals.expected_output: Does not activate Artifact Server publishing because the target is npm, not Artifact Server.
expectations: Does not use artifactserver commands or MCP tools
Does not reinterpret package publishing as an Artifact Server artifact

evals.prompt: Build me a React dashboard with a chart and dark mode.
evals.expected_output: Does not activate publish-artifact because the user asked to build software, not publish finished output to Artifact Server.
expectations: Does not discuss Artifact Server unless the user later asks to publish
Does not invoke the Artifact Server CLI or MCP
